newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firms as liquidity tightens.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht firms as liquidity tightens.

text.p: The Thai baht started the week on a relatively upbeat note after its heavy setbacks late last week, but dealers said offshore players remained wary about the currency's outlook.

The baht was quoted at 25.897-25.901 to the dollar at 0400 GMT against 25.905-25.915 late on Friday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.86 against 25.87 on Friday. "Although the baht/dollar spot rate was still traded very low against the fixing, the central bank's intervention is unlikely today. The market is quite calm this morning," said a senior dealer at a local bank in Bangkok.
Dealers said tightened liquidity in the banking system following the recent dollar buying was triggering some demand for the baht.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 14.50-15.00 percent in early trade.

"I believe the market must be long on dollars against the Thai baht at this point. A lot of people were speculating about a band widening over the weekend and it didn't happen," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
He said continued buying of baht/dollar forwards indicated that sentiment remained weak for Thailand.
Liquidity conditions were the main focus in Indonesia too, where fears about a shortage of funds ahead of the Eid al-Fitr holidays caused the rupiah to firm.
"It's about one-week to the Eid al-Fitr celebration but operators are already getting nervous about liquidity," said a Japanese bank dealer in Jakarta.
"They are afraid of possible higher withdrawals, thus causing people to hold back the rupiah," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,374.75/75.75 at 0400 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,375.8/76.5.
"Dollar/rupiah looks kind of heavy today. 2,376.50 was toppish this morning, but I think it'll hold above 2,372.0/73.0," said the Singapore dealer.
A state bank dealer in Jakarta said it was difficult to estimate how much cash people would need at this stage.
The lunar new year is due on February 7 and the Eid al-Fitr on February 9 and 10. There will be no clearing on February 11.
Dealers said liquidity concerns pushed swap rates up across the board, driving operators to sell spot dollars while looking for a chance to cover through today or tomorrow dollars.
The Malaysian ringgit was confined to a range on a lack of fresh leads as interest began to dwindle ahead of the holidays.
Malaysian markets will close from Thursday to Tuesday to celebrate Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr.
"Dollar/ringgit came down to 2.4800/10 this morning and then went back up. I think it's the work of U.S. funds just selling it down and buying it back," said a Singapore-based dealer.
Some dealers said the ringgit could stand to benefit from a switch in fund flows, as it did last week, if the Thai baht came under renewed pressure.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.4829/39 to the dollar at 0400 GMT against 2.4860/70 at its local close on Friday.
-- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (62-21-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
